item.text: I’ll read the task and starting kernel, then use the harness results to guide the optimization.

The harness confirmed that the starting kernel fails correctness with its placeholder scale. The first revision computes the inverse RMS per row and uses 16-byte loads and stores when the tensors are aligned.
The vectorized revision passed all five cases. The three smaller batches each measured 6.14 µs, so I’ll focus the next comparison on throughput for the two larger batches.

python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p = Path('rmsnorm.cu')
s = p.read_text().replace('rmsnorm_kernel<128, true><<<rows, 128', 'rmsnorm_kernel<256, true><<<rows, 256')
s=s.replace('    __shared__ float scale;\\n','')
a=s.index('    if (warp == 0) {')
b=s.index('    #pragma unroll',a)
s=s[:a]+'''    sum = lane < Threads / 32 ? partial[lane] : 0.0f;
    #pragma unroll
    for (int delta = Threads / 64; delta > 0; delta >>= 1)
        sum += __shfl_down_sync(0xffffffff, sum, delta);
    const float inv_rms = __shfl_sync(
        0xffffffff, rsqrtf(sum * (1.0f / kHiddenSize) + 1e-5f), 0);
'''+s[b:]
p.write_text(s)
PY"
